olders.part: §2 "Phoenix memory has one home; a project pulls the subset it needs": its line "At install, a project pulls a starting set: Garura's rulebook and the memory guide (part 8)" — the install pulls nothing; Phoenix memory reaches a machine the first time the memory tool needs it, downloaded whole from the source its settings name (today a git repository, later a server address) to one place on the machine (default ~/.garura/phoenix-memory), never waiting on a password and stopping after a time limit, and a failed download refuses the lookup with Phoenix memory named; a project's own Garura memory is set up after the install by a new play, `initialize`. The rest of §2 stands (its own git repository, pulling more on need, the list of what was pulled). §3: the line in Kapil's quote "installation is key so that it has some part of LTM build" — Garura memory is built by `initialize`, not the install; until it runs, lookups go up to Phoenix memory; the lookup order and "never blocks a play" stand. §4: "The tool sits outside Garura" — the tool is installed in each project at .garura/tools/memory/ with its settings beside it; agents still call the tool, never a path, so a move to Griffin still changes the tool only. §8 "Every install carries the memory system": the install lays the tool, its settings and the memory guide, brings no memory, and checks that the tool runs and reaches short-term and Garura memory; it does not fail when Phoenix memory is not on the machine yet — it reports it, and notes when the source does not answer. Alternatives Considered: the line "A project pulls nothing at install; every piece on first need" (lost to "a starting set at install") is now the choice for the install.

§1 "Strict .garura/ folder whitelist": the whitelist gains `.garura/tools/`, holding `memory/` — the memory tool as installed, with its settings.json beside it. The tool's own folder is never answered as Garura memory. The rest of §1 stands.
